Four requirements kept returning across the interviews:

Four perspectives from customer discovery
Interview summary / 01

Scalable production

Customers need a process that can grow with demand. Scale-up must preserve useful material performance as production expands.

Customer discovery · Interview synthesis
Interview summary / 02

Affordable cost

Cost needs to fit the intended application. The commercial case depends on producing useful material at a price customers can adopt.

Customer discovery · Interview synthesis
Interview summary / 03

Consistent quality

Customers need dependable material specifications. Consistent output and application-level benchmarks are central to qualification.

Customer discovery · Interview synthesis
Interview summary / 04

Industrial volume

Promising lab results need to translate into reliable supply. Customers require enough usable material to support their production needs.

Customer discovery · Interview synthesis

Four recurring themes from 40+ interviews. Summaries, not direct quotations.

THE COMMERCIAL INSIGHT

Material performance creates interest. Reliable production gives a customer a reason to adopt.

A technology response to those needs

Powerful flow.
Thinner materials.

High-pressure gas generates shear to separate layered feedstock into thinner sheets. Continuous processing and consistent output are development goals.

Customer insight

Entry-market choices

One platform.
Two routes to adoption.

Customer discovery points to two candidate markets, each with a different route to revenue.

GRAPHITE & MINING

Move up the
materials value chain.

Help producers turn layered feedstock into higher-value 2D materials through a gas-driven process.

Candidate business model
Licensing and advisory
What needs validation
Feedstock compatibility, process economics, throughput, and integration.
CONCRETE & RELATED ADDITIVES

Match the material
to the application.

Supply consistent additives for strength, durability, or lower cement use. These applications may not require perfect monolayers.

Candidate business model
Direct sales of 2D materials
What needs validation
Customer specifications, dispersion, dosage, performance, and price.

AN APPLICATION BRANCH

Thermal management adds another test of market fit.

2D-filled polymer composites offer another application to explore: thermal-management components qualified against a user’s performance targets.

Application exploration / technical and supplier qualification still to be established.

Future target

The next validation gate

A pilot that tests
the business case.

A proposed six-month plan turns the remaining assumptions into five practical tests.

  1. 01

    Confirm the need

    Use follow-up interviews to test performance, pricing, volume, and adoption assumptions.

  2. 02

    Choose a pilot partner

    Identify a lead concrete or composites partner with a relevant application.

  3. 03

    Deliver material samples

    Provide CFE output for customer testing under agreed conditions.

  4. 04

    Define and benchmark

    Set product specifications and compare performance with alternatives.

  5. 05

    Plan IP and the pilot

    Begin the IP process and formalize the path to a structured pilot.
